outcome: Migrated Copper-T into the urinary bladder
Stone or encrustation formation on Copper-T
cohort: The study included 7 women aged 21-38 years who were diagnosed with migrated Copper-T IUCDs into their urinary bladders.
finding: Women who have undergone Copper-T insertion with a previous history of C-Section are more prone to have their Copper-T migrated into the urinary bladder.
mod_finding: A history of previous C-Section was found in 6 out of 7 (85.7%) cases of Copper-T migration into the urinary bladder, suggesting a higher propensity for migration in this group.
